newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--The European Union is reportedly preparing a new financing and investment package for Greece that will supercede the Delors II package, Commission President Jacques Santer confirmed yesterday. The new package for 2000-2005 has the in principle agreement of the Greek government, achieved during recent negotiations with the Commission. Santer is in Athens for celebrations commemorating Robert Schumann Day (or "Europe Day") today.

--Greek agriculture is facing serious problems and must become more competitive on a Mediterranean, European and non-European level. Yesterday's Cabinet meeting on the subject reportedly recognised the need to boost the competitiveness of Greek agricultural products, particularly in light of the creation of free trade zones in the Mediterranean.

--A group of Greek diplomats and businessmen visited Skopje in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia yesterday, opening up new prospects for the expansion of Greek investment activity in the neighbouring country.

--Public Order Minister George Romeos yesterday announced new measures to contain the rising road toll. A new police division specifically for traffic on the country's two major highways will be established and the ministry is considering a ban on the movement of lorries during national holidays.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA

--The heads of the country's universities are expected to tell Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis at their weekend meeting that they will shut down their institutions if the government does not go ahead with a law on new wage scales for lecturers.

--Greece's Solidarity Caravan yesterday peacefully distributed 2,000 boxes of food in two Albanian cities, proving that it did not need the protection of soldiers. However, a rebel leader in the region said he would not surrender his weapons.
TA NEA
--Graduates of private vocational schools will be able to go on to state-run technical higher education.
--Park rangers helped two wolves caught in a reservoir escape into the Glafki lake in Larissa yesterday.
--Marlon Brando, the famed actor, will be in Athens later this month to speak on the environment.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--Police yesterday decided on a 48-hour strike, the first in the history of the Greek Police Force, claiming that they are owed pay from 1995.
ETHNOS

--The government is moving ahead with caution to fill vacancies existing in the civil service: the vacancies involve 1,500 more primary school teachers than last year's intake and an equal number of medical staff.
--Greece's sudden introduction to summer got off to a bad start with the first of forest fires on Samos and Evia.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is not considering any changes to the composition of the government, according to reports.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
